steps.what: Read planned recreational activities and current cost evidence
Choose and first record attendance, staffing and activity-cost assumptions
Copy existing actual cost lines into the programme budget workbook
Place verified quantities and rates into programme cost calculations
Write the budget's programme lines and explanatory assumptions
Reconcile budget totals and judge the programme's affordability and assumptions
Save the author's verified programme budget

tasks.design: Configure an {ERP} actual-cost export and a linked {SPREADSHEET} budget template, then reuse its tables in {DOCS}. The manager first chooses and records the programme assumptions, retains unusual calculations and explanatory wording, and personally reconciles the resulting budget; ordinary author saving stays unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget preparation mixes repeated actual-cost copying with new attendance and programme choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports, linked tables and document templates can reuse existing fields without making programme decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Demand, staffing needs and the value of an activity are uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: The manager balances programme quality and affordability and explains the assumptions.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and budget assembly; spending and programme decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a costed programme of activities
reach.learn: Activity costing and explicit demand assumptions

evidence.claim: Native exports and linked budget templates can reuse cost lines and assumptions; this is model knowledge, not a measured recreation-budget case.

assumptions: Boundary is writing and checking the actual programme budget, not a spending release or an unobserved budget presentation. No send or new approval cycle is introduced.

Finance already produces period, cost centre, account, amount and currency in actual-cost records. The manager first chooses attendance, activity quantities, staffing quantities and rates in s2, using actual quotations where needed. Missing or incomparable cost fields are manually reconciled in s6.

Test native exports and templates first. S3 removes fifteen hours of actual second entry. In s4, six of fifteen hours are repeated placement of already captured quantities and rates; nine remain for unusual line calculations and checking. Existing spreadsheet formula runtime earns no saving.
In s5, three of fifteen hours are repeated table layout and headings; twelve remain for first writing of explanatory assumptions. The one-hour same-system author save is fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Whether actual costs already flow into the budget
Comparability of prior programmes and cost categories
research_questions: Can native exports preserve cost periods and categories without manual reclassification?

incremental.description: Maintain cost mappings and test budget template changes

evidence.claim: Saved operational views can reduce navigation before a conversation; this is model knowledge, not an automated conversation saving.

assumptions: Boundary is live coworker communication over radio or computer, not composing a separate staff notice. No new conversation log, action report or trailing record is added.

The programme owner already maintains event identifier, activity, time, place and current status in the actual schedule. The manager reads it in s1 and clarifies missing details during s3; there is no free new staff update duty.

Test native saved views first. Only two of ten lookup hours are repeated navigation; eight hours of reading and context interpretation remain. Selecting the channel and the conversation retain all their time.
The radio is the OTHER workplace-radio category. No autonomous outbound message or internal author save is introduced. Existing call connection runtime earns no saving.

tasks.short: Plan programmes of events and activity schedules

steps.what: Read programme goals and existing venue and activity commitments
Discuss participant needs and confirm activity resources with staff or providers
First record activity duration, resource availability and programme priorities
Plan the programme and place activities into the draft schedule
Check activity times, venue clashes and resource availability
Adjust the event mix and resolve programme conflicts
Save the author's programme schedule

tasks.design: Configure native schedule templates and fixed time, venue and resource-conflict checks in {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}. The manager consults people, first records the actual constraints, chooses the programme mix and resolves substantive conflicts; ordinary saving remains unchanged and publication is not assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated activity placement and fixed clash checks are mixed with creative programme choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Native schedule templates and resource calendars can reuse confirmed activity fields and identify fixed overlaps.
tasks.still_hard: A clash-free timetable may still be a poor or inaccessible programme.
tasks.human_edge: The manager balances audience needs, programme variety and provider constraints.

ambition.what: Compare a second feasible activity sequence when a venue constraint changes

tasks.altitude: Less schedule assembly and mechanical clash checking; programme selection remains a management decision.

evidence.claim: Native resource calendars and activity templates can place repeated fields and check fixed overlaps; this is model knowledge, not a measured recreation-programming case.

assumptions: Boundary is programme and activity scheduling, not staff rostering, external provider commitments or public publication. No new send, report or approval baseline is added.

Existing calendars supply committed venue times and resource identifiers. Staff and providers clarify activity duration, preparation time, availability and participant constraints in s2; the manager first enters and verifies these facts in s3. Missing constraints remain manual, not silently invented by a solver.

Test native templates and conflict checks first. In s4, ten of twenty-five hours are repeated placement of captured times and activity fields; fifteen remain for programme design and individual arrangements. In s5, nine of fifteen hours are fixed overlap checks; six remain for incomplete or unusual constraints.

All substantive adjustment in s6 remains, including repair when automatic checks lack a preparation or accessibility constraint. Ordinary same-system author saving is one fully retained hour and has no self-approval gate.
No model is needed because fixed conflicts and table placement are deterministic; the manager retains all programme judgement.
unknowns: Which activities can reuse existing templates
Whether preparation times and resource identifiers are recorded
Native calendar conflict features already in use
research_questions: Which real clashes can native checks detect without mistaking a feasible schedule for a good programme?

incremental.description: Maintain activity templates and resource constraints after programme changes

Cautious case: a one-off festival requires all twenty-five placement hours because the usual activity template does not fit; fixed venue and time checks still remove nine hours, less two upkeep, giving 7. Consultation, first capture, creative adjustment and saving retain their full time.
